transcript.text: theres water in the bottom of my frige under the salad draws, keeps comming back after i mop it up

That's a very common problem, and the cause is usually a blocked defrost drain. It's normally an easy, free fix.

## Why it happens
Most fridges have a small drain hole at the back wall of the fridge compartment, often just above the salad drawers, sometimes with a little channel or groove leading to it. Condensation runs down the back wall, into the hole, and out to a tray near the compressor, where it evaporates. If bits of food, dust or gunk block the hole, the water backs up and pools under the drawers.

## How to fix it
1. Find the drain hole. Take out the salad drawers and look at the back wall for a small hole, about the size of a pencil.
2. Clear it. Gently poke it with a pipe cleaner, a cotton bud, or a straw. Many fridges come with a little plastic "drain cleaner" tool, sometimes clipped inside the drain hole.
3. Flush it. Use a syringe, turkey baster or squeezy bottle to push warm water (with a little bicarbonate of soda if you like) into the hole. If it drains away freely, it's fixed. If it backs up, keep poking and flushing.
4. If it's frozen (ice in the channel), you may need to switch the fridge off for a few hours with the door open to let it thaw, with towels down to catch the water.

## Other things to check if that doesn't solve it
• Food blocking the back wall: Items pressed against the back panel can stop water reaching the drain or cause ice to build up.
• Door seal: Close the door on a piece of paper. If it slides out easily, the seal isn't tight, letting in warm air and causing extra condensation.
• Temperature setting: Around 3–5°C is ideal. Too cold can freeze the drain.
• Fridge not level: It should tilt very slightly backwards so water runs toward the drain.
• Water dispenser or ice maker (if you have one): A leaking supply line can also cause pooling.

Nine times out of ten it's the drain hole, so start there. If you let me know the make/model I can help you find where the hole is on yours.

ah ok thanks! its a beko fridge freezer, about 4 years old. i took the draws out and theres a little groove and a hole at the bottom of the back wall with bits of lettuce and gunk in it. how do i clear it?

You've found the culprit. Here's how to clear it:

## What you'll need
• Kitchen roll or an old cloth
• A cotton bud, pipe cleaner, or a thin flexible straw (some Beko models come with a little plastic drain-cleaning tool, so check the drain hole and the bag of bits that came with the fridge)
• A syringe, turkey baster, or squeezy bottle (a clean washing-up liquid bottle works)
• Warm water, with a teaspoon of bicarbonate of soda if you like

## Steps
1. Clear out the groove. Wipe the lettuce and gunk out of the channel with kitchen roll so it doesn't get pushed down the hole.
2. Clean the hole itself. Gently twist a cotton bud or pipe cleaner into the hole to pull out any debris. Don't use anything sharp like a skewer or knife, as the cooling pipes run inside the back wall and are easy to puncture.
3. Flush it. Squirt warm water into the hole a bit at a time. If it drains away easily, you're done. If it backs up, poke it again and repeat. The warm water also helps melt any ice in the pipe.
4. Test it. Pour in a small cup of water. It should disappear steadily without pooling.
5. Dry the bottom of the fridge and put the drawers back.

## Optional checks
• The drip tray: If you pull the fridge out, there's a small tray at the back near the bottom (usually sitting on the compressor). Make sure it's not overflowing or cracked. Normally it's dry or nearly dry, since the water evaporates.
• Keep it clear: Every month or two, give the hole a quick poke with a cotton bud and a squirt of warm water. Try to keep salad and veg from touching the back wall, as that's how bits end up in the drain.

If the water keeps coming back after a few days even with a clear drain, let me know and we can look at the seal or temperature next.

ok did that with a cotton bud and warm water and the water went straight down the hole, no more puddle over the last few days. the water was only ever inside the fridge, nowhere near the plug or on the kitchen floor. thanks for your help!

Great news, glad it's sorted! Water draining straight away and no puddle for a few days means the blockage is cleared and nothing else is wrong.

To stop it happening again:
• Give the hole a quick poke with a cotton bud and a squirt of warm water every month or two.
• Keep salad and veg away from the back wall so bits don't wash into the groove.

Enjoy your dry fridge!
